
Three arXiv papers from the last 14 days meet the inclusion criteria. The strongest signal is a paper explicitly about disentangling harness-layer updates from agent capability gains in self-evolving agents — directly on-topic. Two others address context management for long-horizon agents and tool-calling generalization at the harness layer.

## Suggestions

- [Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit: Disentangling Evolution Capabilities in Self-Evolving LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30621) — Disentangles harness-layer scaffold updates from genuine capability gains in self-evolving agents, providing empirical evidence that harness design choices confound agent performance measurement.
  Section: Research Papers > Agent-Computer Interfaces & Scaffolding Design | Criteria: Defines or implements the execution loop, scaffolding, or runtime environment that hosts an AI agent, Evaluates or benchmarks agent behavior through controlled harness-mediated interactions, Empirical or production evidence of harness design improving reliability, safety, or performance

- [Learning Agent-Compatible Context Management for Long-Horizon Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30785) — Proposes a harness-layer context management approach that adapts context handling to agent needs across long-horizon tasks, with empirical evaluation of task performance.
  Section: Research Papers > Context & State Management | Criteria: Manages tool dispatch, context handling, state management, or safety constraints at the harness layer, Defines or implements the execution loop, scaffolding, or runtime environment that hosts an AI agent, Empirical or production evidence of harness design improving reliability, safety, or performance

- [MAVEN: Improving Generalization in Agentic Tool Calling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30738) — Addresses generalization failures in harness-layer tool dispatch for agentic systems, proposing and empirically validating improvements to tool-calling infrastructure.
  Section: Research Papers > Tool & API Integration Layers | Criteria: Manages tool dispatch, context handling, state management, or safety constraints at the harness layer, Evaluates or benchmarks agent behavior through controlled harness-mediated interactions, Empirical or production evidence of harness design improving reliability, safety, or performance
